CBSA reminds travellers of upcoming closure of the Remote Area Border Crossing Program and expansion of telephone reporting
item.description: The Canada Border Services Agency said the Remote Area Border Crossing Program is set to shut at 11:59 p.m. on November 30, 2026. After that date, travellers entering Canada at remote locations will need to call in through designated telephone reporting sites. The CBSA said 17 new telephone reporting sites are already operational, and it has identified more locations after consultations with local and Indigenous communities and other interested parties. Details on the additional sites will be added to the CBSA directory as they open.

RXO latest Curve forecast marks 10th consecutive quarter of spot rate inflation
item.description: RXO's latest Curve truckload forecast shows spot rates, excluding fuel, rising strongly year over year. The index finished the third quarter at 37.9%, up from 32.4% in the second quarter and its highest level since 2021, though rates eased in August and September. Through Nov. 13 the Curve was trending lower on a sequential basis but was still on pace to finish the fourth quarter in inflationary territory. RXO attributed the supply imbalance to ongoing carrier capacity attrition from federal regulation enforcement and rising carrier costs. Jared Weisfeld, chief strategy officer, said overall freight demand remains muted, while the same supply-side pressures are limiting driver reentry.

item.title: Hiring in 2027: How trucking companies can reduce background screening risks
item.description: Vince Pascarella, general counsel for background screening provider Asurint, outlined hiring compliance areas for employers to review heading into 2027. He spoke during the company's Nov. 18 "Keeping Up With Compliance" webinar. He said an employer's headquarters location does not necessarily determine which employment laws cover a worker, so multistate carriers must look at where employees live and work. He cited New York City credit check restrictions and a statewide law that took effect in April 2026 as examples of overlapping rules. Pascarella also described fair chance laws that may require individualized assessments before rejecting applicants over criminal records, and clean slate laws that can seal or expunge records, which may make a new background check differ from an earlier one. On drug testing, he said a positive marijuana test does not necessarily show impairment at the time of an accident. He also named four Fair Credit Reporting Act areas of concern, including adverse action procedures.

East Coast Diesel Stocks Hit Record Low as Trucking Costs Surge
item.description: East Coast diesel supply is the tightest for this time of year on record, according to Department of Energy data reported by Dosya Haber. Inventories fell below 52 million barrels as of last Friday, compared with the roughly 62 million barrels the region typically holds in May. Pump prices have risen with the drop in stocks. The national average reached a record $5.62 per gallon, and the East Coast averaged $5.90, up 63% since the start of the year. Analysts quoted in the report see few signs of a quick turnaround, and say higher prices may remain the main way to draw more fuel cargoes into the Northeast.

Annual Thanksgiving tradition serves truck drivers free meals at Boise Stage Stop
item.description: The Boise Stage Stop has provided free Thanksgiving meals to truck drivers for decades, according to KBOI. Connie Gepner, who has worked at the stop for 28 years, said the aim is to show appreciation to each driver who comes in on the holiday. Each driver also gets a goodie bag containing movies, beef jerky, chargers and a raffle entry. Gepner said staff work on Thanksgiving so the meals can be served, and the stop plans to keep the tradition going for years.

Coaldale, Lethbridge County release results of 2-month commercial vehicle inspections
item.description: Community peace officers in Coaldale and Lethbridge County have released results from a joint round of commercial vehicle safety inspections carried out in September and October. Over those two months, inspectors completed 15 inspections and identified a few problem areas involving brakes, tires, load securement and general vehicle equipment. Coaldale Mayor Jack Van Rijn, in a media release, thanked the two municipalities for working together and said keeping commercial vehicles up to safety standards protects everyone on the roads.

CBSA seizes over $25 million in nicotine products across Southern Ontario
item.description: Canada Border Services Agency officers at land ports of entry across Southern Ontario seized more than $25 million worth of illicit nicotine products over four days in November. The products were in commercial freight coming in from the United States. The agency said the seizures help disrupt organized crime, and the federal government said it is investing $1.3 billion to strengthen border security and the immigration system under its Border Plan.

Dolly Parton and the Tennessean Truckstop
item.description: The writer describes a recent visit to the Tennessean Truck Stop in Tennessee, which now operates as Dolly's Tennessean Travel Plaza. The original independent stop burned down in 2021, and a replacement opened in early 2024. The rebuilt site has a truck lot the writer says has reportedly room for 200 trucks, plus a new lounge with recliners, showers and laundry. Most of the main retail space is filled with Dolly Parton merchandise. Quoting a review from Miles 2 Go, the writer says the site is a travel stop more than a truck stop.

Melton driver honored as TCA Highway Angel for helping four crash victims in Kentucky
item.description:
The Truckload Carriers Association has named Sammie Phillips, a driver for Melton Truck Lines, as a TCA Highway Angel. Phillips was driving near Lexington, Ky., at about 8:10 a.m. on Aug. 14 when an SUV carrying four young adults rolled several times in front of him. He turned on his emergency lights, pulled over and ran to the wreck, then climbed onto the vehicle, which had landed on its side, to try to reach the occupants.
Two occupants told him they were injured, and the other two had scrapes and bruises. Law enforcement arrived shortly afterward and helped get them out, while Phillips stayed to give officers information. The TCA said nearly 1,500 drivers have been recognized since the program began in 1997, supported by presenting sponsor EpicVue and supporting sponsors DriverFacts and Northland Insurance.

DOT watchdog refers 20 motor carrier cases for prosecution in 6 months
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Transportation's Office of Inspector General referred 20 motor carrier-related cases for criminal or civil prosecution between April 1 and Sept. 30, 2026, according to its semiannual report to Congress. Six of the cases involved falsified or altered inspection records, six involved fraudulent registrations or chameleon carriers, and one each involved attempted bribery, CDL violations, drug and alcohol program violations and driver qualification issues.
The report highlights a Louisiana CDL bribery scheme that ran from 2020 to 2024 and let more than 100 people obtain licenses without meeting requirements, with more guilty pleas reported in September. Separately, FMCSA expanded its online complaint center earlier this month to give industry members more ways to report suspected fraud and safety violations.
